source_version: Theory of Computing15(2019),Article6; final publisher source October11,2019
title: Computable dimension reduction preserving Gaussian partition noise stability approximately

standard_prerequisites.name: Gaussian analysis, Hermite expansions and finite-dimensional tensor algebra
standard_prerequisites.statement: Original stated background/citations and all local partition regularization, polynomial/tensor reconstruction and stability arguments retained.
standard_prerequisites.use: No collector proof of cited background results; no efficient/primitive-recursive dimension claim or negative-correlation extension.

core_obligations: The authors regularize arbitrary Gaussian partitions to polynomial threshold partitions, control surface area and rounding while retaining noise stability, then reconstruct low-dimensional polynomial systems through tensor decompositions, multilinearization, mollification and quantitative sign/collision control. The complete local dimension-reduction construction is retained. Original computable (not primitive-recursive) dimension, approximate part-measure preservation and positive-noise parameter are explicit.

editorial_notes: Complete original author body/proof and bibliography retained. Part measures are preserved up to epsilon as stated; no exact-measure or negative-correlation strengthening. Original computable n0 is explicitly not primitive recursive.
